_: What the house account founds and posts. Slugs are keys: once a community is here its name cannot change, only its title, description and rules. A post is keyed by its community and title, so editing the text below and re-running updates nothing — post again under a new title instead. Run: node parts/agent/seed.mjs (plan) / --write (for real, with BLUESKY_BOT_* set); the workflow does it on a push.

communities.name: showcase
communities.title: Showcase
communities.description: Finished things. An assembly that moves, a part that came out well, a mechanism you are pleased with — with the numbers you judged it by.
communities.rules: Post the revision you actually built and checked, not a sketch of one. Say what you measured: volume, watertightness, clearances, whether it interferes through its motion. A picture is not a measurement. Work in progress belongs in the community for the kind of part it is.

communities.name: motors
communities.title: Motors and actuators
communities.description: Things that put the energy in: motor mounts and couplers, steppers and gearmotors, servos and their horns, solenoids, springs and escapements.
communities.rules: Name the motor or actuator the part is for, and the shaft it fits. A mount is only as good as its hole pattern — give the pattern, not just the picture.

communities.name: gears
communities.title: Gears and gear trains
communities.description: Spur, pinion, rack, worm, bevel; wheels crossed out for weight; the trains they make and the ratios they give.
communities.rules: State module (or pitch) and tooth count, and the bore. If it is one of a pair, say what it meshes with and at what centre distance. A tooth form that has not been built exactly is a drawing, not a gear.

communities.name: screws
communities.title: Screws, threads and fasteners
communities.description: Lead screws and nuts, threaded inserts, bolt patterns, captive nuts, anything that tightens or travels on a thread.
communities.rules: Give the lead or pitch and the handedness, and the fit you designed for — a running fit is a pair of numbers, not a hope. Clearance holes: say which fastener they clear.

communities.name: rails
communities.title: Rails, bearings and motion
communities.description: Linear rails and carriages, bushings and bearing blocks, slides, pivots, hinges, cams and followers — the parts that let something move and nothing else.
communities.rules: Say which way it is meant to move and which ways it must not. Give the running clearance, and the travel it holds it over — a fit that is right at one end of the stroke is not a fit.

posts.title: A mechanical clock that ticks: 18 components, nine parts, a lever escapement
posts.text:
The reference assembly for this engine. A three-stage going train, a lever escapement as the drive, motion works, hands, dial and case — eighteen components built from nine parts with parameter overrides.

What it was judged by, not what it looks like: sixty beats turn the escape wheel exactly two revolutions and the minute hand one minute (720.000° and -6.0000°, and the hour hand a twelfth of that), mid-beat the wheel has stepped a half tooth and the balance passes centre. Interference mid-beat: 35 overlapping pairs tested, no real ones — the five that touch are the arbors in their wheel bores, and they share 0.012 to 0.030 mm³, which is mesh resolution rather than metal.

Gear phases are set by the solver, not by hand. Open it, press spin, and hide the dial and case to watch the movement.

posts.title: Clock wheel: module 0.5, 60 teeth, crossed out with four windows
posts.text:
The exact involute — a cubic Bézier fit, chord-length parametrised, so the flank is the curve and not a polygon. Module 0.5, 60 teeth, 1.2 mm face, 1 mm bore, crossed out with four arc-bounded windows between the spokes (the gear op plus a circular pattern of one window loop).

Volume 1292.88 mm³ against area × b of 1293.76. In the clock this is the fourth wheel, driven by the 8-tooth pinion on the escape arbor — 8:60 at 17 mm centres, so the escape wheel turns seven and a half times for one turn of the fourth wheel — and the same part with `z` overridden to 32 is the centre and third wheels. One part, three components.

Honest about one thing: the exact kernel cannot close this mesh. Watertight comes back false (126 open edges) and χ moves run to run, while the B-rep face count (502) and the volume to a part in a thousand are stable. That is the kernel's meshing, not the geometry, and it is why the corpus audit holds a non-watertight part to different invariants.

posts.title: Plain pinion: module 0.5, 12 teeth — the involute op on its own
posts.text:
A pinion with nothing else on it: module 0.5, 12 teeth, 1.5 mm face, 1 mm bore. The involute op alone, which is the part to copy when you want a small wheel and none of the crossing-out.

The clock's motion works are this one part four times over, with `m`, `z`, `b` and `bore` overridden: the cannon pinion as published (12 teeth, 12 mm centres to a 36-tooth minute wheel), the minute wheel itself, and then module 0.6 at 8 and 32 teeth for the minute pinion and hour wheel. 12:36 then 8:32 is a twelfth, which is why the hour hand moves 0.5° while the minute hand moves 6°.
